summary: Registers an ENUM service for SIP, focused on putting SIP addresses-of-record under telephone numbers. It follows RFC 3761 and was updated by RFC 6118.

eli5.summary: This lets a phone number point to someone's internet phone address so calls can be routed to them.

questions: map phone number to sip address
what is a sip address of record
how does enum map phone numbers to sip
address of record vs contact address
subtitle: Registers the E2U+SIP ENUM service so a telephone number can point to a person's SIP address.

tldr.problem: ENUM turns telephone numbers into URIs through DNS, but there was no registered service type for pointing a number at a SIP identity.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers the E2U+SIP enumservice, whose NAPTR records hold a sip: or sips: address-of-record, meaning a long-term user identity rather than a particular device.
tldr.outcome: Phone numbers can map to SIP addresses, and SIP's own capability negotiation still happens afterwards. RFC 6118 later updated this RFC.

today: RFC 3764 is a Proposed Standard and is listed as updated by RFC 6118. It has not been obsoleted according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: ENUM and SIP
sections.content:
ENUM (E.164 Number Mapping) uses DNS to translate telephone numbers like +12025332600 into URIs such as sip:egar@example.com. It exists mainly to connect systems that rely on telephone numbers with those that use URIs to route transactions. This document applies to the revised ENUM described in RFC 3761.

SIP (RFC 3261) is a text-based application protocol that lets endpoints find one another to exchange context about a session. It sets up things like Internet telephony, instant messaging, video and Internet gaming.
sections.eli5: ENUM is a phone book on the internet that turns a phone number into an internet address. SIP is the way internet calls get started.

sections.title: The Registration Template
sections.content:
Following the template in RFC 3761, the RFC registers one enumservice. Its fields are:

  • Enumservice name: E2U+SIP
  • Type: SIP, with no subtype
  • URI schemes: sip: and sips:
  • Intended usage: COMMON
  • Author: Jon Peterson

The IANA section says the registration is made in the enumservice registry described in RFC 3761.
sections.eli5: This is the form filled in to get a new service name added to the official list.

sections.title: Addresses-of-Record and Contact Addresses
sections.content:
The key idea is the difference between two kinds of SIP URI. A contact address belongs to one device, such as a SIP phone, and may look like sip:10.0.0.1. An address-of-record is a long-term identity of the user with no dependency on any device, generally a simple URI like sip:edgar@example.com. The RFC compares it to the difference between a device and its user.

A caller puts the target's address-of-record in the To header field and generally the Request-URI. A device sends a registration to a registrar to temporarily associate its contact address with the user's address-of-record, and proxy servers then ask a location service where to find the user. Addresses-of-record can even be registered under other addresses-of-record, so a home identity can be directed to a work one.

To find the right server, a SIP entity ordinarily resolves the domain part of the URI using the mechanisms of RFC 3263.
sections.eli5: An address-of-record is like your name, and a contact address is like the chair you are sitting in right now. People want to reach you, not the chair.

sections.title: Why Not List Device Capabilities
sections.content:
An address-of-record has no capabilities as such, because it names no particular device. When a SIP user agent sends a request to one, a rich two-way negotiation begins, using SDP, Required and Supported headers and optional extensions.

ENUM's capability management is one-way. The telephone number's administrator lists protocol names and preferences that the client must evaluate without negotiation. The RFC argues that a NAPTR service field cannot express session details down to codec level, and that putting contact addresses in ENUM would compromise SIP's discovery and negotiation. If ENUM wanted to target particular devices, it says, E2IPv4 would be a more appropriate service to define than E2U.
sections.eli5: A phone book entry can only say a few simple things. Working out the best way to talk is better left to the two sides when they connect.

sections.title: The E2U+SIP Enumservice
sections.content:
The services field of a NAPTR record normally has a protocol subfield and a resolution service subfield. ENUM defines the E2U (E.164 to URI) resolution service, and this RFC defines E2U+SIP for SIP.

The URI in the regexp field of such a record may use the SIP or SIPS scheme. The SIPS scheme, when used in an address-of-record, indicates that the user can be reached only over a secure connection using TLS. The enumservice is best suited to addresses-of-record, which need no further capability data. There is also generally no need for more than one such NAPTR record under a single telephone number.

The user part of a SIP URI may itself contain a telephone number, such as sip:+1442079460148@example.com. Clients should be careful to avoid infinite loops when recursively performing ENUM queries on URIs that result from an ENUM lookup.
sections.eli5: The phone book entry says: for this number, use the internet-phone address given here. You only need one such entry per number.

sections.title: An Example Record
sections.content: The RFC gives one NAPTR resource record using the new enumservice. Under a domain derived from a telephone number in e164.arpa, it holds the service string E2U+sip and a substitution expression that returns sip:edgar@example.com for any input. The record is shown in the figure.
sections.eli5: Here is one real-looking phone book line: for this number, the person is at this internet address.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
Placing a SIP address-of-record in ENUM is comparable to placing an email address or similar URI in DNS. DNS makes no policy decisions about who may see its records, so all records must be assumed to be available to all inquirers at all times. ENUM record sets must therefore be considered public, which raises some privacy considerations.

On the positive side, the resource a SIP URI identifies may require callers to present cryptographic credentials before the user is alerted. The RFC concludes that ENUM combined with SIP can give far greater protection from unwanted callers than the existing PSTN, even though ENUM records are public. Threats specific to ENUM's dependence on DNS, and the applicability of DNSSEC, are analysed in RFC 3761.
sections.eli5: A phone book is open to everyone, so anyone can see the entry. But an internet phone address can ask callers to prove who they are first.
